claims.claim: The criminalization of jaywalking resulted from an aggressive 1920s campaign led by auto groups and manufacturers that redefined who owned city streets.
claims.episode_span: The change followed intensive lobbying by automobile manufacturers and local motor clubs who argued that pedestrians, not drivers, were the main source of collisions.
claims.source_title: The forgotten history of how automakers invented the crime of "jaywalking" - Vox
claims.supporting_quote: it’s actually the result of an aggressive, forgotten 1920s campaign led by auto groups and manufacturers that redefined who owned the city streets.

claims.claim: The scholarly anchor for this history is Peter Norton, historian at the University of Virginia and author of Fighting Traffic: The Dawn of the Motor Age in the American City.
claims.episode_span: Automakers recast streets as car space and turned crossing them into a crime, reshaping cities for a century.
claims.source_title: The forgotten history of how automakers invented the crime of "jaywalking" - Vox
claims.supporting_quote: a historian at the University of Virginia and author of Fighting Traffic: The Dawn of the Motor Age in the American City

claims.claim: "Jay" was 1920s slang for a rube or hick, and pro-auto groups promoted "jay walker" to ridicule pedestrians as people who did not know how to behave in a city.
claims.episode_span: a term popularized by auto-club publicity that labeled mid-block crossing as rural ignorance
claims.source_title: The forgotten history of how automakers invented the crime of "jaywalking" - Vox
claims.supporting_quote: During this era, the word “jay” meant something like “rube” or “hick” — a person from the sticks, who didn’t know how to behave in a city. So pro-auto groups promoted use of the word “jay walker” as someone who didn’t know how to walk in a city, threatening public safety.

claims.claim: Los Angeles enacted strict pedestrian controls in 1925, and the 1928 Model Municipal Traffic Ordinance was largely based on Los Angeles traffic law.
claims.episode_span: Los Angeles adopted one of the earliest strict statutes in 1925
claims.source_title: The forgotten history of how automakers invented the crime of "jaywalking" - Vox
claims.supporting_quote: the product of those meetings — the 1928 Model Municipal Traffic Ordinance — was largely based off traffic law in Los Angeles, which had enacted strict pedestrian controls in 1925.

claims.claim: Auto industry groups took control of a series of national traffic-safety meetings convened by Secretary of Commerce Herbert Hoover to create a model traffic law for cities.
claims.episode_span: The National Conference on Street and Highway Safety, convened in 1924 under Secretary of Commerce Herbert Hoover, brought together traffic engineers and safety advocates
claims.source_title: The forgotten history of how automakers invented the crime of "jaywalking" - Vox
claims.supporting_quote: auto industry groups took control of a series of meetings convened by Herbert Hoover (then secretary of commerce) to create a model traffic law that could be used by cities across the country.

claims.claim: Newspaper coverage of street deaths flipped from blaming drivers in 1923 to blaming jaywalking by late 1924, under an auto-industry-fed reporting service.
claims.episode_span: Newspapers ran safety campaigns funded by motor interests that showed cartoon “jays” darting into traffic and being struck
claims.source_title: Jaywalking: How the car industry outlawed crossing the road - BBC News
claims.supporting_quote: The newspaper coverage quite suddenly changes, so that in 1923 they're all blaming the drivers, and by late 1924 they're all blaming jaywalking

claims.claim: Virginia was the first state to decriminalize jaywalking, with the reform taking effect in early 2021 from legislation passed in 2020.
claims.episode_span: Recent state-level reforms in places such as Virginia (2020) and California (2022) have decriminalized mid-block crossing when it can be done safely
claims.source_title: The Progress of Jaywalking Reform - America Walks
claims.supporting_quote: The state of Virginia kicked things off by decriminalizing jaywalking in March 2021, followed by Kansas City, Missouri one month later.

claims.claim: On September 30, 2022, California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the Freedom to Walk Act decriminalizing jaywalking in California.
